entities.summary:
Íñigo Fernández de Velasco, 2nd Duke of Frías, was a Spanish nobleman who played a significant role in the politics of Castile during the Late Renaissance.

Born in 1462, Fernández de Velasco rose to prominence as a trusted advisor to King John II of Castile, serving as Constable of Castile from 1494 to 1502. His influence extended beyond the royal court, shaping the policies of the Spanish monarchs and contributing to the rise of the Spanish Empire.

Fernández de Velasco's legacy extends beyond his lifetime, as he laid the groundwork for the consolidation of Spanish power in the Americas and the Mediterranean. His leadership during the Spanish-Portuguese wars of succession also had a lasting impact on the political landscape of Europe.

Despite his significant contributions to Spanish history, Fernández de Velasco remains a lesser-known figure, overshadowed by more prominent contemporaries. Nevertheless, his impact on the trajectory of Spanish power and influence cannot be overstated.

As the 2nd Duke of Frías, Fernández de Velasco embodied the ideals of the Spanish nobility, upholding the values of loyalty, duty, and service to the crown. His dedication to his lord and country earned him a lasting place in the annals of Spanish history.
